Hello all,

I would like to create an overlay plot for observed (open circle) and predicted (line) values, where I also want to differentiate two predictions.

The problem is, I want to show only open circle for observed data in the legend.

 

Here is a small dataset to create this problem:

116L, 117L, 118L, 119L, 120L, 121L, 122L, 123L, 124L, 125L, 126L,

127L), class = "data.frame")

 

 

df <- melt(df,

            id.vars =c("ID","Time"),

            measure.vars = c("Observed","Pred1","Pred2")

            )

 

 

#this is closest what I want, but need little more trick.....

 

ggplot(df, mapping=aes(x=Time, y=value, group=variable, colour=variable, linetype=variable, size=variable)) +

              geom_point(data=subset(df, variable=="Observed"), shape=1) +

              geom_line(data=subset(df, variable=="Pred1")) +

              geom_line(data=subset(df, variable=="Pred2")) +

              facet_wrap(~ID, ncol=3) +

              scale_colour_manual("", breaks = levels(df$variable), values = c("black","red","blue")) +

              scale_linetype_manual("", breaks =levels(df$variable), values = c(3,2,1)) +

              scale_size_manual("", breaks =levels(df$variable), values = c(2,0.5,1.2))

 

 

I don’t want to show line in the legend for observed data, so I tried ‘NULL’ as below:

scale_linetype_manual("", breaks =levels(df$variable), values = c(NULL,2,1))

 

but it doesn’t work (‘NA’ doesn’t work either).

 

Is there any way to remove the line (only for the observed data) in the legend?

I searched online spending couple of hours, found a similar problem post, but it didn’t answer my question…I may missing some information, but I really appreciate if someone help me on this.

Thank you very much.

Hello again,

I am still seeking for help to create a plot (legend) below with ggplot.

I can do it in lattice but was not successful with ggplot. The issue is, I need ‘point’ for observed data and ‘line’ for predicted data in the legend, as shown in the plot.

 

With lattice, I can create a legend (key) like this (the data (df) is before ‘melt’. The example dataset is in my previous email below):

 

library(lattice)

head(df)

  ID  Time Observed  Pred1  Pred2

1  1 24.00        0  0.000  0.000

2  1 30.92       16 20.732 19.023

3  1 32.10       19 17.952 16.418

4  1 32.12       14 17.907 16.376

5  1 33.10       11 15.796 14.425

6  1 34.10       10 13.866 12.652

 

xyplot(Observed + Pred1 + Pred2~Time |as.factor(ID), data=df, ylab="value", layout=c(3,1)

       ,type=c("p","l","l"), col=c("black","red","blue"),

      ,lty=c(0,2,1), lwd=c(0,1,2), pch=c(1,0,0), distribute.type=TRUE,

       key=list(space="right", cex=0.6

            ,text=list(c("Observed","Pred1","Pred2"), col=c("black","red","blue"))

              ,lines=list(type=c("p","l","l"), lty=c(0,2,1), lwd=c(1,1,2), pch=c(1,0,0),col=c("black","red","blue"))

              )

       )

 

 

Since I haven’t  heard from anybody so far, I am guessing it is probably not possible to have different types (shape and line) in the same legend with the current version of ggplot…..? Could anybody comment on this? And if so, is it possible to add it to the wish list for the next version, because I believe people want to have this type of legend when we create a plot with points and lines in the same plot…..

 

I appreciate your feedback.

Kaori
